turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come, sit. What has brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing much, doctor. The face is looking a little odd on one side, that is all. I said not to come.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It is not nothing. From morning the left side of his face is hanging. I saw it when I brought the tea.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Hanging, she says. A small droop only.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): When exactly did it start?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): When I woke, uh, around six. Mirror showed the left side down. Nothing in the night.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you able to close the left eye?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, almost. Why, it is a small gap only.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): No, doctor, it stays open. I have been watching. He is not blinking that side.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine, it is not closing all the way. Happy?
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): And can you whistle?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Whistle is not coming today. Left lip will not join. Usually I can.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): So I have this right: since this morning the left face is drooping, the left eye will not close fully, you cannot whistle, and you are calling it mild.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Mild. It should go by itself.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weakness in the arm, or in the leg?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No weakness. Arms are strong, legs also no problem.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Speech? Any slurring, or the wrong words coming?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Speech is perfect. You are hearing me no.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any pain in the ear, or behind the ear?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Yesterday a little pain in the left ear. Today it is gone. I never even took a tablet.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He was pressing the ear the whole of last night. Morning he told me the pain stopped.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Anyway, coming here itself was a project. Traffic from Whitefield, one and a half hours, silk board completely stuck.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Such heat also. I told her the match is tonight, India batting second, why spoil the evening.
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He started on the team with the auto driver. Then the grandson phoned, seven years, shouting he took a wicket in the gully match.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I was laughing only. Then rain for five minutes and that auto had no wiper. We just sat there.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. We can come back to cricket after. Eyebrows up, please.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right forehead wrinkles. Left forehead is not moving at all.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Now shut the eyes hard. The left eye stays open, the eyeball is visible. The right closes.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Smile for me. Mouth pulls to the right, left fold by the nose is flat. Grip my fingers. Both arms equal, I do not find any weakness.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Speech while we talk is clear, no slurring.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pressure just now is 146 over 88. Pulse 78, regular.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Last month at the shop it was 130 only. This is traffic tension, nothing else.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The nurse outside checked before we came in. She told me 148 over 90. He had said to her also that it is always 130.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): 130, 148, all fine.
[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): One thing, doctor. He does not take the BP tablets on Sundays. I have seen the strip sitting there.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Arre, not Sunday. Saturday I skip, and that also sometimes only. Sunday I take it. You have mixed the day.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Name and dose of that tablet?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipin, err, five mg, morning, for the BP. The BP itself is there for ten years.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Amlodipine 5 mg every morning for blood pressure, present for ten years, and you sometimes leave out Saturday, not Sunday.
[SEG0040] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Also he sleeps badly. Night after night he is awake, turning. I hear from the other room.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): That is not true. I sleep very well. She makes a drama.
[SEG0042] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Last month he cut his finger cutting beans. The cut healed in five days, fully normal. I am only saying.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Healed in five days, so not a slow-healing wound. I will not chase that. Any headache, double vision, chest pain, trouble breathing, pain in the stomach?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No headache, no double vision, chest fine, breathing fine, stomach fine.

[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will tell you my impression, provisional only. This is a left Bell's palsy, the facial nerve. I am not calling it a stroke. The forehead is involved and the arm and the speech are spared.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Then leave it no? It will settle. Why a big medicine.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am starting prednisolone 60 mg once daily, by mouth, for five days, morning with food. When you return I will set the taper. Short course, this is the usual dose.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): 60 mg for a little droop. Too much. But okay, if you insist.

[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): The eye can dry because it will not close. Lubricating drops in the left eye every two hours while you are awake. At night, ointment and tape the eyelid shut. Do not skip the taping.
[SEG0050] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will do the drops and the tape. He will argue and I will still do it.

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Amlodipine every morning, Saturdays included. And I will see you in one week. If the arm becomes weak, or the speech changes, or a severe headache comes, go to emergency the same day, do not wait.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): One week, fine. It will be gone before that. Come, the match is at 7.

[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me set it out once. Left face droop since morning, eye not shutting, cannot whistle, ear pain yesterday now gone, no arm weakness, no speech trouble. Prednisolone 60 mg daily for five days, eye drops and night tape, amlodipine every day, review in one week.
[SEG0054] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Thank you doctor. I will keep the tablets out in the morning.

spec.situation: Person woke with one side of the face drooping, cannot close the eye, cannot whistle; no arm weakness, no speech problem, ear pain a day before; doctor examines and starts steroids, eye care explained.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

bad.reason: Left ear pain yesterday, mild and resolved are supported; duration '1 day' is not stated.
bad.text: Left ear pain (category=ENT, status=resolved, severity=mild, duration=1 day, onset=yesterday, temporality=resolved, body_site=left ear, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Route/body site for lubricating drops and ointment: lubricating drops are for the left eye every 2 hours while awake; ointment is also for the eye at night with eyelid taping, and the doctor emphasized not to skip the taping.
Prednisolone was specifically to be taken in the morning with food.
Amlodipine 5 mg was specified as taken in the morning.
On eye closure exam, the left eyeball was visible when attempting to shut the eyes hard, while the right eye closed.
Smile exam details: mouth pulled to the right and the left nasolabial fold was flat.
Both arms had equal grip strength on examination.
The doctor noted no slow-healing wound based on the caregiver's report that a finger cut healed fully in five days.
The doctor explicitly stated he was not calling this a stroke.
